qs.q: The following Mendelian disorders are autosomal recessive except one. Which one?
qs.e: Hereditary spherocytosis is autosomal dominant (~75% of cases). The others are autosomal recessive.
qs.s: MCQ: Genetic Disorders Year 3 End Year

qs.q: : A couple has a child with an autosomal recessive disorder. Neither parent is affected. What is the probability that their next child will be affected?
qs.e: In autosomal recessive inheritance, two carrier parents have a 25% chance with each pregnancy of having an affected child (homozygous recessive), 50% chance of a carrier, and 25% chance of being unaffected and not a carrier.

qs.q: Which statement about autosomal recessive disorders is INCORRECT?
o: They include almost all inborn errors of metabolism
Onset is frequently early in life
qs.e: In autosomal recessive disorders, parents are typically NOT affected but are carriers. The trait manifests in children who inherit two mutant alleles.

qs.q: A 4-year-old girl presents with recurrent lung infections and pancreatic insufficiency. Sweat chloride test is positive. This autosomal recessive disorder is caused by mutations in which gene? Classic cystic fibrosis presentation. ---
qs.e: Cystic fibrosis is caused by mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator gene.
qs.s: Pathology by Dr. Irungu — MCQ Bank

qs.q: A child born to phenotypically normal parents develops cystic fibrosis. The inheritance pattern is most consistent with: Two unaffected carrier parents having an affected child is the hallmark of autosomal recessive inheritance. ---
qs.e: An affected child born to two unaffected carrier parents is the characteristic hallmark of autosomal recessive inheritance.
qs.s: Pathology by Dr. Irungu — MCQ Bank

qs.q: If a couple are carriers of an autosomal recessive trait, what is the probability that all their four children will be homozygous for the disease? Each pregnancy independently has a 1/4 chance; probability of *all four* being affected multiplies the independent probabilities. ---
o: Probability equal to one hundred percent
Probability equal to one quarter to fourth power
Probability equal to one minus sum of quarters
Probability equal to sum of four quarters
qs.e: Each independent pregnancy carries a 1/4 risk for an autosomal recessive disease, so all four children being affected multiplies individual probabilities.
qs.s: Pathology by Dr. Irungu — MCQ Bank

qs.q: Which of the following features distinguishes autosomal dominant from autosomal recessive inheritance? This vertical pattern is classic for AD; AR instead shows generation skipping (e is a description of AR, not a distinguishing feature stated as such). ---
o: Vertical transmission with affected parent in each generation
Equal gender involvement across all affected pedigree lines
Homozygosity required for clinical expression of disease
Skipping of generations throughout affected family trees
Requirement of both parents to carry the mutant allele
qs.e: Autosomal dominant disorders typically show vertical transmission with an affected parent present in each successive generation.
qs.s: Pathology by Dr. Irungu — MCQ Bank
